payload.text: **EVERY NEW STACK DECISION THE DAEMON INTRODUCES IS RULED AND RECORDED BEFORE IT IS ADDED, TO THE STANDARD THIS WORKSPACE ALREADY HOLDS.** **THE COUNT IS DERIVED FROM THE LOCK AND IS NOT WRITTEN HERE.** An earlier wording said *three*, fixed at a moment when a template layer was still in the stack; D56's reversal removed it hours later and the literal would have gone stale in a criterion nobody re-read. **A criterion that names a number instead of deriving one rots silently** -- third instance on this thread, after a row that stated a count and a row that stated line numbers. Measured 2026-08-29 (cc, verified by vc): the lock carries **no async runtime, no server and no filesystem watcher** -- zero rows for tokio, axum, hyper, actix-web, async-std, smol, tower, notify -- and `intentd/Cargo.toml` has no `[dependencies]` section at all. `async-graphql` is present and has only ever been used SYNCHRONOUSLY for the SDL export, so it pulled no runtime in. **So the additions WP-08 makes are this workspace's firsts of their kind**, and the check is that each dependency added to `intentd` carries a written rationale -- `uuid` carries three paragraphs explaining its addition alongside `ulid` -- **with D06's rusqlite prohibition surviving all of them.** The rationale may cite the sibling estate rather than re-argue from scratch: `../Conflab`'s `conflabd` runs tokio and axum on a 127.0.0.1 management plane whose `mgmt/` module is 10,341 lines including 3,648 of tests.
